subject: [hw] R1 finding F1 (V14, HIGH): CBZ/CBNZ with i=1 (offset >=64) return UNDEF and lose bit 6
body:
File: gpu/hwcodec/emu/n2a32_t16.c:324 and :332 (dispatch), :196-205 (t16_misc_cbz).

Bug: the CBZ/CBNZ test is `(w & 0xF700u) == 0xB100u`. The T1 encoding is 1011 0 op i 1 imm5 Rn (ARM ARM A8.8.30/A8.8.31): bit 11 = op (CBZ/CBNZ), bit 10 = 0, bit 9 = i, bit 8 = 1. Masking with 0xF700 requires bit 9 (i) == 0, so every CBZ/CBNZ whose branch offset has bit 6 set is not claimed and falls through to the "reserved holes" return N2A32_UNDEF at :343. Also t16_misc_cbz ignores bit 9 entirely, so even if it were claimed the target would miss i<<6.

Repro (built against the current tree, stubs only for n2a32_mmio_*):
  llvm-mc: `cbz r0, far` at 0x10 with far=0x58 encodes 0xB310 (llvm-objdump: b310 cbz r0, 0x58 @ imm = #0x44).
  c.r[15]=0x1004; c.next_pc=0x1002; c.thumb=1; c.r[0]=0;
  n2a32_t16(&c,0xB310) -> rc=1 (UNDEF), next_pc=0x1002. Expected rc=0, next_pc=0x1048.
  Same for cbnz i=1: 0xBB10 -> rc=1.

Why it matters: the D01 census counts cbz=4429, cbnz=744 in the vendor set; any forward branch >= 64 bytes or backward branch is affected. This stops the interpreter on ordinary compiled code, so it is a blocker for integration, not a corner case.

Fix: use a mask that ignores bits 11 and 9, e.g. `if ((w & 0xF500u) == 0xB100u)` (0xF500 = bits15-12=1111, bit10=1, bit8=1), and in t16_misc_cbz add the i bit: `imm = ((w >> 3) & 0x1F) << 1 | ((w >> 9) & 1) << 6; target = c->r[15] + imm;`. Please add a test with 0xB310/0xBB10 (i=1) and a negative offset (e.g. cbz r0, .-0x40) to test_v14.

Severity: high (wrong decode of a common instruction, silently stops execution). I will re-check when you post the fix.
